(1) MALAT1 and HOTAIP are two lncRNAs that are involved in the regulation of the ER signaling pathway in prostate cancer; (2) MALAT1 acts as an inhibitor of the ER signaling in prostate cancer; and (3) HOTAIR acts as an activator of ER signaling in prostate cancers.
HOTAIR and Malat1 long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) are involved in estrogen receptor (ER) action in prostate cancer cells.
HOTAIR and the MALAT1 long non-coding RNA (lncRN) are recruited to estrogen-responsive genes and are regulated by estrogen in prostate cancer cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the mechanisms of action of the lncRNA HOTAIR and the lncRNA MALAT1 in estrogen signaling.
the study of the mechanisms that regulate the expression of long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) in human cancer.
the role of lncRNAs and their involvement in estrogen signaling in prostate cancer cells.

MALAT1 and HOTAAR are both involved in estrogen-mediated regulation of gene transcription but with opposite roles.
HOTAIR is a positive regulator of estrogen signaling while MALAT1 is a negative one.
HOTAIR is an activator of estrogen signaling while MALAT1 is an inhibitor of the same pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in prostate cancer, the lncRNA HOTAIR is a negative regulator of ERα function while MALAT1 is a positive regulator.
in prostate cancer estrogen signaling involves the recruitment of HOTAIR on chromatin, while MALAT1 is recruited in the unstimulated state.
